title: Churn Triage & Simulation Handbook — Exec Escalation Kit
summary: Working handbook for running churn-triage tabletop simulations, a lightweight QBR template focused on early renewal signals, and an exec-escalation kit with templated comms and mitigation play actions.
audience: CS leads, AMs, customer success ops, GTM leadership
objectives: Create repeatable quarterly simulation runs that surface blind spots in renewal workflows
Provide a tight QBR template for early warning signals and recommended save plays
Define clear exec-escalation triggers and a lowest-friction communication cadence
Ship a compact renewal tracker schema that AMs can update in under 10 minutes per account
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working kit — half runbook, half toolkit — intended to help CS teams run fast, realistic renewal-risk simulations and to standardize the path from detection -> AM play -> exec escalation. Keep it intentionally lightweight so teams actually run it.

Quick notes / how to use:
- Run the simulation quarterly for the top 50 At-Risk accounts (by ARR).
- Use the QBR template (below) during the next cadenced customer meeting if possible, otherwise run as a synthetic call with stakeholders.
- After each sim, capture 3 immediate takeaways and 1 action owner.
- This is deliberately blunt: prefer a short list of high-impact actions to a long laundry list.

Section A — Triage scoring (one-page):
- Inputs (AM fills): status, last-activity, exec-contact-health, product-usage-trend, tech-incidents-last-90d, support-volume, contractual-exposure (months to renewal), CS-sentiment (qualitative).
- Quick scoring rubric (0-10 each, AM provides a score):
  * Engagement (0 none -> 10 highly engaged)
  * Outcomes alignment (0 misaligned -> 10 strong outcomes)
  * Product health (0 repeated P0s -> 10 buttery smooth)
  * Financial exposure (0 <3 months -> 10 >12 months) [inverse mapped when calculating risk]
  * Executive involvement (0 no exec contact -> 10 regular EBRs)
- Risk score = weighted sum (weights: Engagement 0.25, Outcomes 0.25, Product 0.2, Financial 0.15, Exec 0.15), normalized to 0-100.
- Triage band mapping: 0-39 = Low, 40-64 = Medium, 65-79 = High, 80-100 = Critical.

Section B — Simulation scenarios (run in 60-90 minutes):
- Prep (15 min): pick 2 real accounts, collect the last 6 months of usage, SRE incidents, NPS verbatims, AM notes.
- Roleplay (45 min): assign roles (AM, Customer Exec, Product SME, Finance), run scenario A and B (below), capture decisions and timelines.
- Debrief (30 min): list assumptions that broke, missing data, immediate playbook changes.

Scenario A — Quiet taper (most common):
- Signal: steady drop in monthly tokens/usage over 90 days; AM has not engaged on new initiatives; contract renewal in 5 months.
- Objective: test detection -> early outreach -> re-alignment conversation -> propose two save plays (commercial and product).
- Play outcomes to test: usage analysis appears later than customer signals; AM schedules solutions call within 10 days; product SME identifies simple friction (adapter config) fix that can be shipped in 3 weeks; commercial offers short-term credit tied to feature adoption metrics.

Scenario B — Escalating technical failure (high urgency):
- Signal: repeated latency/regression bugs, multiple support P1s in 45 days, legal looped in. Renewal in 9 months.
- Objective: test cross-functional rapid response and exec escalation (when to pull VP/GM into the thread).
- Play outcomes to test: SRE-driven mitigation plan, short-term SLA concession, executive outreach within 48 hours, weekly status updates to the customer, commit to technical remediation timeline before next billing cycle.

Section C — Entry criteria for exec escalation (goes directly to VP/GM and CRO):
- Any account in Critical band (>=80) AND >$250k ARR OR strategic (platform integrator, multi-product).
- Any account with unresolved P1s >72 hours AND renewal within 12 months.
- Any contract with active legal notice or at-risk litigation that could impact go-forward terms.
- Manual escalation: AM or TAM can escalate earlier if exec relationships are at risk (use rationale in thread).

Escalation process (fast path):
1) AM fills one-line brief (use template below) and posts to #cs-escalations Slack with tag @vp-cs.
2) Schedule 30-min triage with VP/GM within 24 hours; invite product and SRE SMEs.
3) Agree on 3 deliverables and owners with target dates (48 hrs / 7 days / 30 days).
4) Exec outreach: prescriptive email + 15-min intro call; no broad promises on pricing without finance ok.

One-line brief template (AM to post to Slack):
- Subject: Escalation request — <Account> — RiskScore=<score> — Renewal=<mm/yyyy>
- TL;DR: 1-2 sentences on why at risk (usage down, P1s, legal).
- Ask: what do we want (exec connect, committed fix, concession)?
- Impact: ARR, product bundles at risk, reference value.
- Attach: triage-sheet link + last 3 NPS verbatims + topo map of customer org.

Sample Exec Email (send after triage call):
Hi <ExecName>,

Following a review, our team has flagged a material renewal risk for <Account>. We’d like 15 minutes to align on remedial steps and discuss prioritization from our side.

Key context: <one-liner>.
Requested: 15 min call this week to confirm remediation plan and executive sponsorship.

We will follow up with a concrete 30/7/48 plan after the call.

Best,
<AM Name>

Section D — QBR template (lightweight — fill in under 10 minutes):
Fields (AM to copy into meeting notes):
- Account name
- ARR and committed spend
- Renewal date
- Customer success owner + exec sponsor
- Top 3 outcomes customer cares about (bullet list)
- Last 90d usage trend (up/down %), critical incidents (count)
- Open deliverables (owner + eta)
- Risk score (auto-calc from triage sheet)
- Recommended save plays (1 commercial, 1 product/process)
- Next steps (owner + date)

Section E — Save plays library (examples to pick quickly):
- Commercial: short-term term credit tied to adoption KPIs (90 days), extension of pilot pricing for feature set, commit to tiered discount if usage rebounds.
- Product: prioritized bug fix, temporary capacity bump, dedicated onboarding resource for 30 days.
- Process: weekly working sync for first 30 days then biweekly for 90 days, shared success metrics dashboard.

Section F — Renewal tracker schema (one-row-per-account; AMs keep up-to-date):
Columns (CSV-friendly):
- account_name, arr, renewal_date, days_to_renewal, risk_band, triage_score, last_checkin, last_exec_touch (date), open_p1_count, open_deliverables_count, owner, next_step, next_step_due, notes_link

Minimum update cadence: once per week for Medium+, twice per week for High/Critical.

Section G — Simulation lab cadence & roles:
- Runbook owner: CS Ops (owns scheduling and data export).
- Facilitator: CS Lattice (rotates quarterly).
- Participants: AM, TAM, SRE rep, Product PM, Finance rep (optional), Exec reviewer for Critical scenarios.
- Deliverable after each run: 1-page run-debrief with decisions and updated tracker rows.

Section H — Post-escalation follow-up checklist (for the first 30 days):
- Day 0: Exec outreach + confirm 30/7/48 deliverables.
- Day 2: Product/SRE mitigation plan shared with customer.
- Day 7: Commercial options presented; decision documented.
- Day 14: First adoption checkpoint; quantitative check vs agreed KPIs.
- Day 30: Executive readout and next milestone plan.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Need a one-click extraction from our usage dashboards to populate the triage sheet — CS Ops ticket to analytics (JIRA-CS-5032).
- How do we better detect quiet tapers earlier? Can we add a 3rd party signal (infra spend or API error spikes)?
- Validate commercial concession approval flow with finance for pilot credits.

Appendix — Quick links:
- Sim lab confluence page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/renewal-sim-lab
- Triage sheet template: (link to sheet)
- Slack channel: #cs-escalations

Contact / owner: Ivy Chen (ivy.chen@redwood.ai) — reach out if you want a dry run or need facilitation.

Working draft — expect edits. This should be practical, not perfect. If it feels heavy, trim it.
